facts.content: Patient has upper lip swelling after eating prawn soup, worsening.
facts.source_text: CC: Upper lip swelling after eating prawn soup ~19:00; worsening

facts.content: The swelling started approximately 30 minutes after ingestion, beginning at the left upper lip corner and progressively increasing.
facts.source_text: Onset ~30 min post-ingestion; started at left upper lip corner → progressive swelling

facts.content: Patient experienced dyspnea and possible throat tightness.
facts.source_text: Dyspnea; possible throat tightness; uncertain chest tightness

facts.content: Patient felt dizziness during the call.
Patient has a history of asthma.
Patient has a peanut allergy with a childhood severe reaction.
facts.source_text: Allergies: Peanut (childhood severe reaction per mother; possible prior injection/hospital visit)

facts.content: Had a similar allergic episode about a year ago with late-night Chinese food, causing swelling and breathing difficulty.
facts.source_text: Prior similar episode ~1 yr ago after late-night Chinese food with swelling and breathing difficulty

facts.content: Patient uses a Salbutamol inhaler and takes occasional antihistamines, though unsure of the specific type.
facts.source_text: Meds: Salbutamol inhaler; occasional antihistamines (unsure which)

facts.content: Suspected anaphylaxis secondary to shellfish (prawn) exposure, presenting with acute lip angioedema, dyspnea/throat tightness, dizziness, with a history of peanut allergy and asthma.
facts.source_text: Suspected anaphylaxis secondary to shellfish (prawn) exposure: acute lip angioedema, dyspnea/throat tightness, dizziness; hx peanut allergy and asthma; prior similar reaction.

facts.content: Asthma is noted, and patient only uses SABA.
Emergency services (999) to be called; patient advised not to be alone and instructed to have mother call.
facts.source_text: Emergency services (999) to be called; advised not to be alone; mother present to call

facts.content: Patient advised to take any available antihistamine while waiting for the ambulance.
facts.source_text: Take available antihistamine while awaiting ambulance

facts.content: Urgent evaluation in the emergency department is necessary with a possible need for intramuscular adrenaline and monitoring.

facts.content: Post-discharge follow-up with a GP for epinephrine autoinjector education and supply, and for allergy referral/testing.
